methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer that has raised $51.6M to date. The sector comprises 9 peer companies (1 public, 8 private), including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics, though narrow peer comparables at the same stage and valuation tier are insufficient for robust median benchmarking.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis is the applicable method. Using total raised ($51.6M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.2x step-up multiplier for late-stage advancement yields an implied value of $61.9M. The peer-median approach cannot be reliably applied; the broader robotics sector contains 10 companies, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables returns fewer than three datapoints, which would introduce unacceptable selection bias.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $53M to $71M, with a median of $62M. This range reflects upside from stage progression while acknowledging the difficulty in precise calibration absent tighter peer data. Key uncertainties include commercialization trajectory, competitive positioning within the fragmented robotics sector, and whether public comparables (277810.KQ) represent meaningful benchmarks for Kinova's specific applications and market maturity.
